newsitem.title: UK: Repsol confirms Tarragona petchem cracker restart.
newsitem.headline: Repsol confirms Tarragona petchem cracker restart.

text.p: Spain's Repsol SA restarted its 550,000 tonnes a year ethylene cracker in Tarragona at the weekend after an outage of "some days", a Repsol petrochemical marketing source said Monday.
But a source at Dow Chemical Co said the U.S. producer's 500,000 tonnes a year Dutch cracker at Terneuzen could be down until August 15, having suffered compressor damage during a July 27 outage.

Naphtha market players said that the outages at the large-scale crackers had come close to wiping out the already limited prompt/August demand for naphtha, the main feedstock used in European petchem cracking.

The Repsol source said the Tarragona unit, cited as the main cause for concern in naphtha markets, suffered production problems for six days until its restart Saturday, with the outage accounting for some of those days.
The Dow source said he expected Terneuzen, which has been down since July 27, would be "back up and running anytime from August 12 to 15."
